medhx: Type 2 diabetes, Hypercholesterolaemia, Chronic kidney disease
notes: PSA 11.2 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.18. Prostate volume 61 mL. csPCa 0.85.

note_sections.t: Evaluation initiated after documenting a sustained PSA elevation alongside a previous biopsy result establishing ISUP grade group 4 malignancy.

A 64-year-old factory supervisor, currently cohabiting with his partner after a divorce, seeks re-assessment of a known prostate malignancy. His PSA values have climbed steadily from 3.3 ng/mL in early 2023 to the present 11.2 ng/mL. Underlying type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease are managed with metformin and empagliflozin, while hypercholesterolaemia is addressed through a combination of atorvastatin, simvastatin, and rosuvastatin. His estimated glomerular filtration rate has held steady beneath 60 mL/min/1.73m2. Urological discomfort is negligible, reflected by an IPSS score of 4, and he denies any blood in the urine or voiding difficulties. A significant smoking background of 29 pack-years ended in 2001; alcohol consumption remains limited to four units per week. He favors weekend gardening over formal exercise routines. Recent non-urological care included a standard chest radiograph and an audiology check for mild age-related hearing shifts, alongside a persistent sleep disturbance he links to occupational stress. Due to residing over ninety minutes from the clinic, he has asked that telephone consultations be utilized whenever medically suitable.

Digital rectal assessment: Normal DRE — prostate measures approximately 60 g with a smooth, firm consistency and no detectable nodules or asymmetry.
Systemic evaluation shows no abnormalities. Vital parameters remain stable at a blood pressure of 99/73 mmHg and a heart rate of 81 bpm. Body mass index registers at 31.7, aligning with his reported activity levels. Peripheral lymph nodes are non-palpable, and suprapubic regions exhibit no tenderness.

admin: Lives >90 min from clinic; phone follow-up preferred where clinically safe.
